summary.final_text:
The Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample ran and the plate was read at 595 nm. Well A1 gave an absorbance of **0.3207**.

What I did:
1. Picked up a tip, aspirated 10 µL of unknown protein sample (reagents:A4), dispensed it into assay_plate:A1, and dropped the tip.
2. Picked up a fresh tip, aspirated 200 µL of Bradford dye reagent (reagents:A3), dispensed it into assay_plate:A1, and dropped the tip.
3. Read assay_plate at 595 nm.

The other wells on the plate read about 0.03–0.06, which is background level. I did not run a BSA standard curve, so I can't convert the 0.3207 reading to a protein concentration. If you want a concentration, the BSA standards (reagents:A2, 2 mg/mL) would need to be run on the plate the same way.

task_def.source: Bradford microplate procedure as in Bio-Rad Bulletin 2674: 10 uL of sample plus 200 uL of diluted dye reagent per well, absorbance read at 595 nm.
task_def.prompt: Run a Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample: in assay_plate well A1, combine 10 uL of the sample with 200 uL of Bradford dye reagent, then read the plate at 595 nm.
